Welcome, Timekeeper!

Every financial statement tells the story of a business. For that story to be accurate, every transaction must be recorded in the right chapter, at the right time. A company that records revenue too early, or forgets to record an expense it has already incurred, is not telling an accurate story. Investors, lenders, and managers rely on these numbers to make real decisions. Your job in Chapter 3 is to make sure the story reflects reality, not just what is convenient.

WHAT TO EXPECT

1
Adjusting Entry Scenarios (5 Qs): Use a visual timeline to identify when revenue is recognized, then apply adjusting entries
2
Accrual Basis Concepts (5 Qs): Analyze the principles behind accrual accounting and evaluate their real-world effects
3
Effects of Omissions (5 Qs): Identify what happens to the financial story when adjustments are skipped
4
Completing the Cycle (4 Qs): Closing entries, permanent accounts, and the matching principle
